title: The coach sticks to what it gets right
summary: The coach no longer gives economy advice, and it drops claims it cannot back up.

items.text: The coach no longer covers the economy. Reviews and Ask Coach stop giving buy, save and money advice, and an economy question gets a plain answer that it is not covered.
Ask Coach drops claims it cannot back up: a won pistol round nobody mentioned, habits stated about a whole map, and a Marshal body shot that only kills an unarmoured player.
Better advice on map control and on reading where the enemy will go next.
The Recording screen says no tips or advice until the match ends, since it now shows your map, agent, score and round.

title: More motion, and chart numbers that stay off the line
summary: The app moves with more care, and the numbers on your grade charts no longer sit on the line.

items.text: The app has more motion: the tab marker glides between pages, numbers count up, lines draw themselves, bars grow, and pages and lists rise in once when you open them. Reduced motion in Windows turns all of it off.
Buttons press in when you click them, and switches slide between choices.
The numbers on your grade charts on Home and Matches no longer sit on the line.

title: Four free games, and a note when games arrive
summary: Free is now 4 games, everyone gets 2 more, and a card tells you when a gift or new games arrive.

items.text: Free is now 4 games for life, 6 with an invite. Every account gets 2 more, including players who already used theirs.
When someone sends you a gift, an invite pays off or new games arrive, a card slides in to tell you. It waits until your match ends.
Your account menu opens as a dropdown from your avatar, over the page.
Home shows your Riot ID, the K/D of your last match, and plays the fix clip right there.
Stats shows more of your numbers: combat score, K/D and damage a round, where your shots land, your maps and your acts.
The Patterns chart is easier to read: one colour, lines for each grade letter, your average, and whether your last match was above or below it.
Recording keeps the AI log on, because the review needs those frames to look at your deaths. Turning recording off now asks first.
The times under the Matches chart no longer run together, and the wins and losses count is gone.

title: A new look, and a live status while you play
summary: A new look with a top bar, and a live status of your Valorant match on the Recording screen.

items.text: A new look across the app. The sidebar is replaced by a top bar with your pages, the game switch and your account menu, and Home, Matches, reviews and Settings are redrawn.

While a Valorant match is on, the Recording screen shows its map, your agent, the score and the round, with a strip that draws the rounds as they go. Each one has a switch in Settings, and nothing else about the match is shown until it ends.
Maps have their own art on Home and in reviews.
Ask Coach no longer drops a correct answer about how many hits a gun needs to kill through armor.
With no match attached, Ask Coach reads the round you describe and picks advice that fits it far more often.

title: The previous look is back, and the coach checks more of what it says
summary: The app looks the way it did before 8.8.0, and reviews and Ask Coach check six more kinds of claim against Riot's record.

items.text: The app is back to its previous look. The notebook redesign from 8.8.0 is gone.

Reviews and Ask Coach now check six more kinds of claim against Riot's record: where you died, which rounds the coach looked at and how many, whether you died more than you killed, lists of rounds that do not match their count, and utility your team does not have, like a drone.
Ask Coach gives better advice on holding an angle with a sniper, buying on pistol, eco and team save rounds, retakes and defusing, and reading which site the enemy will hit next.
With no match attached, Ask Coach no longer talks about what a record shows.

title: A coach's notebook, and fewer wrong claims
summary: The app looks like a coach's marked up notes, and reviews check what they say about your rounds more strictly.

items.text: Review, Home and Matches are redesigned like a coach's notebook, with the one thing to fix in bold, hand drawn pen marks on the rounds that prove it and a margin for times and grades.
Buttons now have three clear ranks, one main action per screen, and press down a little when you click them.
Counts in reviews and Ask Coach, like how many deaths nobody traded, now come from one list, so they no longer contradict each other or call a death alone when Riot shows a teammate close.
A round where Riot marked you AFK is now left out of your grade, your missed list, your patterns and your Moments, not only your repeated mistakes.
Ask Coach answers aim questions from your own numbers with drills you can really do, and the RR on your reviews keeps trying until Riot publishes the game.
A review no longer loses its round lines when a player in your match has a name that contains a word like aim.

title: Where you died, and what you bought
summary: Linked round cards now show where each death happened, what your team bought and how close a teammate was.

items.text: When your match is linked to Riot's record, each round you died in shows the spot, like B Main, and whether a teammate was close enough to trade you.
Each linked round shows your team's buy, from pistol to full buy, and longer matches count how your team did on full buys, ecos and forced buys.
Reviews of your recent ranked matches show the RR you gained or lost, and Stats adds your peak rank and your all time aces and clutches from Riot's record.
The coach picks advice from where you died and how you bought, and a round where Riot marked you AFK says so on its card and is left out of your repeated mistakes.

Reviews and Ask Coach check what they say about a round, where you died, the plant and how close a teammate was, against Riot's record, so fewer mistakes reach you, and higher ranks get advice that fits them.
Reviews saved before this update look exactly as before.

title: A coach that reads your match, not a checklist
summary: Reviews and answers now lean on what your match and your own history show, with sharper advice at every rank.

items.text: Reviews pick the lesson that fits your rank and your match, and only lead with trading when it keeps costing you across your matches.
Higher ranks get advice built on their match's real numbers, like a side that kept losing or a post plant that kept failing.
Ask Coach answers practice, aim and improvement questions with your own biggest lever instead of the same habit every time.
The coach no longer gets agent abilities wrong, quotes stats it cannot check, or leaves half sentences behind.

title: Sharper, more honest coaching
summary: Reviews and Ask Coach now focus on what really decided your match, answer the question you asked, and check their facts harder.

items.text: Your review now leads with the change that would help you most, like a side you kept losing or a player who kept killing you, not the same habit every time.
Ask Coach answers what you asked: aim, practice, climbing or how to play into an agent, with notes picked for that question.
Aim is judged from your own numbers, and a death in a round you lost is no longer praised just because it was traded.
Advice at higher ranks goes deeper than advice at lower ranks, not just longer.
The coach no longer mixes up ability keys or makes up details the match record does not show, and it answers basic questions it used to refuse.

title: A coach that knows the matchup
summary: More coaching from top players, advice that knows who you played against, and worked examples for the moments that decided your match.

items.text: The coach learned 133 more habits from top coaches and Radiant players, with much more for Ascendant and above.
Matchup advice: when the enemy had a Killjoy, a Viper or another agent that changes how you play, the coach tells you how to play into them.
When a moment in your match looks like one top players handle well, the coach walks you through what to notice and what to do.
Lower ranks now get the fundamentals that matter most at their level first, while higher ranks keep the deeper advice.

title: Report a problem, and advanced coaching for everyone
summary: Tell us when something goes wrong with a picture and a few words, and get the deepest coaching that fits your rank by default.

items.text: A Report a problem button above the Discord icon. Describe what went wrong, add up to 3 pictures and send it straight to us.
Advanced coaching is now on for everyone. It goes deeper while fitting your rank, so you never get advice meant for a rank above yours. You can still turn it off in Settings.
Ask Coach no longer tells you your rank back, it just fits its advice to it.

title: Gifts, clips in Ask Coach and a smarter coach
summary: Gift Pro or Max to a friend with a link, watch your own clips inside Ask Coach, and get advice that fits your rank.

items.text: Gift Pro or Max for a month or a year. You get a link to send, and your friend redeems it in one click.
Ask Coach can show the clips it is talking about, right under its answer.
Each round you died in shows who killed you, with their agent, weapon and the damage they did.
A Discord button in the sidebar and a What's new page in Settings.
The coach learned from top coaches and Radiant players, and its advice now fits your rank.
Your Verdict shows your agent and your standout stat of the match, like an ace or a clutch.
Rounds are cleaner, without the row of small frames under each clip.
Free games are now one set per player.

title: Ask Coach and your games
summary: Ask Coach now follows your games, with a clear way to get more when you run out.

items.text: When you have used all your games, Ask Coach says so in one calm line with a button that opens your Profile.
Games you buy unlock Ask Coach straight away.
Ask Coach takes one question at a time and slows down questions sent very fast.
Reviews and Ask Coach answers come from newer AI models that matched the old ones in our tests and cost less to run.
Occlara's servers now guard every request against floods, so the coach stays up for everyone.

title: Your Profile, and buying games
summary: A new Profile page shows your games left, lets you buy more and sums up how you play.

items.text: A Profile page in the sidebar, between Invite and Settings, with your games left as the first thing you see.
Buy more games from the app at $2 a game, any number from 1 to 500. Games you buy never expire.
Your play in Valorant at a glance: your most used weapon, your most played agent and your peak rank.
The Free, Pro and Max plans side by side, monthly or yearly.
The coach's notes were checked and corrected, and it reads the latest patch notes again.
A chosen option in a switch no longer turns invisible when you hover it.
Your match library rebuilds itself if its index is ever damaged, so no review is lost.
A revive no longer counts as a clutch.
Spike Rush matches are read correctly, halves included.
A round end countdown is no longer mistaken for a death.
An update never restarts Occlara in the middle of a match.
Round pictures in a review show again instead of a broken image.

title: Highlights for every multikill
summary: Every round with two or more kills is now a highlight, and reviews read in plainer sentences.

items.text: Every round where you get two or more kills is saved as a highlight, named 2K, 3K, 4K or 5K, alongside clutches and first kill streaks.
Reviews are written in short plain sentences, without semicolons.

title: Accounts, a new look and Moments
summary: Sign in with your browser, start with 2 free games, and meet a calmer Occlara with the new Moments page.

items.text: Accounts: sign in through your browser. A licence key still works too.
Free, Pro and Max plans. Free gives you 2 games for life, Pro 25 games a month and Max 70 a month.
An Invite page. Each friend who signs up with your link gets 2 extra free games, and you earn 4 games per friend, up to 20.
Moments replaces Breakdown: every death and highlight from your matches in one place, with Play all for each repeated mistake.
A new look across the whole app: one calm column, clean lines instead of boxes, and the fix for your next match as the biggest line.
A lighter 480p recording size for modest PCs, which used about a quarter less CPU than 720p in our tests.
Reviews open with a Verdict you can share as an image, and show how you did against your last match and your average.
Milestones on Home and in Matches mark your bests and the habits you have cleared.
A match played with no games left is still saved in your library with Riot's record of it.
Invited friends get their extra games even if they confirm their email later.
League of Legends is marked coming soon while we finish it. Your League reviews are kept.

title: The crescent
summary: A new crescent mark and one cleaner look across the app.

items.text: A new crescent logo, with tray icons for light and dark taskbars.
Matches, Stats, Settings and reviews share one cleaner look.
The close button in the first run setup sits inside its card again.
